title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Boomtown Arts & Heritage FestAVL
location: Pack Square Park
description:
Boomtown Arts & Heritage FestAVL proudly announces its return for a third year, set for September 4 – 6, 2026, at Pack Square Park in the heart of downtown Asheville. The free, all-ages festival celebrates Western North Carolina’s local music, regional culture, and architectural history with multi-genre main stage performances, interactive family programming, and heritage trail tours. 
FESTIVAL SCHEDULE – ALL FREE WITH RSVP 

Friday, September 4: 3:00 PM – 10:00 PM
Saturday, September 5: 10:00 AM – 10:00 PM
Sunday, September 6: 10:00 AM – 10:00 PM

We’re bringing back some of your favorites along with some fresh talent. The newly released 2026 lineup is colorful and eclectic, leaning into funk, jam, and global rhythms. Pack Square Park’s stages host Lettuce for two sets, plus Cimafunk, Groundation, Toubab Krewe & Friends, Golden Dawn Arkestra, Empire Strikes Brass, Jon Stickley Trio, StephanieSID, Electro Lust, Jonathan Scales Fourchestra, Atash, Wolph, New Dawn Starkestra, The Jlloyd Mashup, Auspicious Golden Fish, Suns of Stars, Las Montañitas, Black Sea Beat Society, Adama Dembele & Les Amis, Coconut Cake, and Dancing Drum. For lineup updates, RSVP information, and festival news, visit www.boomtownfestavl.com. 
Asheville emerged as a boomtown in the 1920s as the city rebuilt following “The Great Flood” of 1916 – an era that produced some of the most monumental pioneers, visionaries, poets, and architecture of its time. When the stock market crashed in 1929, the city’s commitment to repaying its debt preserved that historic architecture, leaving Asheville a remarkable snapshot of a turn-of-the-century boomtown. One century later, Boomtown Festival honors that legacy while helping rebuild a thriving community in the wake of Hurricane Helene – driving festival revenues directly back into key organizations fostering measurable progress in the communities hindered most by the boom-year debts, and highlighting their stories of resilience. 
FESTIVAL HIGHLIGHTS 

Main Stage Performances: Three stages featuring 30+ global, regional and local artists across a dynamic mix of genres. 
Asheville Symphony in the Park: The beloved tradition of accessible classical music returns Sunday, September 6.
“The Big Secret” Family Stage: Sunday, September 6 – a day of family programming with collaborative sets from local acts, plus surprises for kids and families.
Heritage Tours & Exhibits: Explore Asheville’s architectural legacy and historic boomtown origins through curated trail tours and displays.
Wellness Pavilion: Free yoga, mindfulness sessions, and holistic wellness demonstrations.
Local Artisan Market: Handmade goods, culinary offerings, and crafts from regional vendors.
Local Food Vendors: Global flavors made locally 
Children’s Zone: Arts and crafts, storytelling, and interactive play activities for the whole family.

Join us for an unforgettable celebration that bridges the past and present, fostering a deeper connection to Asheville’s vibrant legacy.

title: Flat Laurel Creek Rock Scramble
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
This is one of the most popular creek scrambles near Asheville. Note this is not the Flat Laurel Creek Trail, it is a creek hike. It begins at NC Hwy. 215 near the confluence of Flat Laurel Creek and the West Fork of the Pigeon River (35.3285, -82.9096), approximately, at about 9:30. We will ascend past numerous rapids and impressive waterfalls. We will be in the creek or rock hopping most of the day. The requirements are a good sense of balance, comfortable shoes with good traction, and ability or interest to scramble up rocks in a creek. We'll also climb a steep trace trail *around* the highest waterfall. Good swimming holes abound. The pace will be moderate, with time for pictures, and we will take a short break at one of the many scenic spots for lunch. After finishing the ascent we will trail hike up to the Black Balsam/Big Sam parking lot, where cars will be left for this shuttle. You will have the option to hike up Big Sam Mountain (over 6K) for the view. However, the group will proceed directly to the parking lot for Big Sam.
We will climb 950 feet and hike approx. 3.5 miles.
We will be meeting at the end of Black Balsam Knob Road (FS 816) at the parking lot for the Big Sam trailhead at 9:05 am. The coordinates are 35.325586, -82.881986.
Any questions I can be reached or text at 828 231-3581.

**LEGALESE**
This Asheville Hiking Group (AHG) event involves serious risks, including but not limited to: slipping or falling on wet rocks; sprains, fractures, and other injuries from falls; water-related injury; exposure to weather, cold, or heat; wildlife encounters; remote locations with limited or delayed access to emergency medical care; and risks arising from my own or other participants' actions. These risks cannot be eliminated regardless of care taken. Participants are responsible for their own safety and affirm that they have the appropriate skills, physical conditioning, equipment, and supplies. Neither your hike organizer nor Asheville Hiking Group can assure your safety nor eliminate all risks. Participants assume full responsibility for any damages, losses, or injuries.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Salamander Diversity in the Southern Appalachians
description:
Salamander Diversity in the Southern Appalachians
with Patrick Brannon 
Saturday, September 5  |  1 – 3:30pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
  
The southern Appalachians are one of the most biologically diverse regions in the temperate world. More species of salamanders exist in these mountains than anywhere else, and nowhere are they more abundant. Participants will be presented a lecture focusing on biology and ecology of salamanders, biogeography, reasons for the enormous diversity in this region, and local threats to species diversity. Afterwards, students will analyze and graph data to observe how different species coexist in streams. Weather permitting, we will then search the Arboretum grounds to observe species in the wild. 
Patrick Brannon is an independent naturalist and educator. He holds a M.S. in Biology from Appalachian State University, and has performed research on the ecology of salamanders and small mammals. For the past 22 years he was Outreach Coordinator at the WCU Highlands Biological Station, where he taught courses on amphibians and mammals as part of the UNC Institute for the Environment Program at HBS, in addition to many K-12 school programs and educator workshops.

title: Wool Spinning Demonstration with Jamie Sparks
location: NC
description: Jamie Sparks is a multidisciplinary artist and educator with more than 30 years of experience teaching learners of all ages. She has spent more than two decades working with natural fibers, specializing in spinning and felting, and has taught throughout the Southeastern U.S., including the John C. Campbell Folk School, Tryon Arts and Crafts School, assisting at Penland School of Crafts and numerous arts councils.  Her fiber arts instruction emphasizes the transformation of raw fleece into finished pieces, combining traditional techniques with an accessible, hands-on approach. Jamie holds an Associates in Metalsmithing from Haywood Community College, where she developed her skills in metalwork and design. Prior to her work in the arts, she focused life as a herbal educator and plant biologist with a focus on the relationship between humans and plants—a passion that continues to influence her creative practice.

title: Scenic AVL Wildcard - Asheville Camino
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**Overview:** This hike is offered as a monthly training hike with the WNC Asheville Chapter of the association of American Pilgrims on the Camino. The route has been announced on the WNC Camino Group [Facebook Group Page](https://www.facebook.com/groups/AVLCamino/announcements).

See details here: [https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1DSW8LYBvx/](https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1DSW8LYBvx/)

**12 Mile Route**
Isaiah will be leading the full 12 mile route around west Asheville through Malvern Hills and back along Haywood. Isaiah and his wife created the route many years ago when they were training for their first Camino. It's amazing to see how the tradition of urban hiking has grown in Asheville as a result of their original training hikes. Here is the route that Isaiah will lead: [https://www.alltrails.com/explore/custom-routes/avl-camino-frances-west-loop-7bb5b06?u=i&sh=ifwm3x](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/custom-routes/avl-camino-frances-west-loop-7bb5b06?u=i&sh=ifwm3x)

**7 Mile Route**
I will be leading the shorter option of 6.75 miles, which will start with the full group, and then turn up the road that overlooks the French Broad River. We will stop for coffee at Wrong Way Campground at the 3.4 mile mark.
All Trails Route for SHORTER option: [https://www.alltrails.com/explore/custom-routes/copy-avl-camino-frances-west-loop-3645ccb?u=i&sh=ifwm3x ](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/custom-routes/copy-avl-camino-frances-west-loop-3645ccb?u=i&sh=ifwm3x)

**Elevation Gain: 600 ft**
Both routes have about the same elevation gain (down to the river and back).

**What to bring:**
Payment method for coffee or snacks. For the longer hike, there will be a brief lunch stop near a market where you can buy a sandwich or eat a sandwich you bring with you. Carry adequate water.

**There are NO BATHROOMS at the start, so plan accordingly.**

This hike will count as a weekend wildcard on my Scenic Asheville series. There are 9 hikes in the series; hike them all and receive an attractive badge for your backpack.

Guests: This is a good hike to bring a guest, because it's not as hard as some others. If you bring a guest, remind me of their name at the end so that they will get credit for the hike.

**Camino FAQ**
The Camino de Santiago is an Unesco world heritage route followed by pilgrims for centuries. If you are unfamiliar with the Camino, here are a few links to learn more:
\*[American Pilgrims on the Camino](https://americanpilgrims.org/iwpmap_directory/western-north-carolina/)

* [Stingy Nomads Camino](https://stingynomads.com/camino-de-santiago-walking-guide/)
\*[Gronze Camino Planner](https://www.gronze.com/)

When we stop for coffee, you can ask all the questions you want.

Disclaimer and Release of Liability:
This activity involves hiking on city streets that may have traffic. Participants are responsible for their safety on streets and trails. The organizer of this trip is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this trip. If you sign up or participate in this event you acknowledge that you freely and voluntarily agree to assume all risks of injuries, illnesses, and damages arising from, as a result of, and associated with this event. In addition, you acknowledge that you agree to the Meetup terms: [https://www.meetup.com/terms](https://www.meetup.com/terms)

title: Crystal Pyramid Sound Healing
description:
Awakening Asheville
Release and reset with a heart-centered sound bath layered with crystal beds, a pyramid, crystal light chakra balancing and energy healing!

Experience a unique and transformative sound bath journey and more! In this deeply nurturing and restorative sound bath, you will receive the additional healing benefits of lying on a full-length cushioned bed of infused amethyst crystals, with the option of lying inside our crystal-filled heart chakra pyramid or under the infused chakra balancing crystal lights. The space is anchored with many crystals, plants and a heart-centered energy that is both nurturing and magical. Group size is small so that each person can start their journey by experiencing the cleansing energy of standing inside a Tibetan foot bowl while its being played. This opens and clears your energy field to receive and drop more deeply into the experience.

Come relax, reset and remember the peace that you are as the soothing waves of many sacred sound instruments wash through you. There is nothing you have to do or prepare for, just come as you are and experience a variety of crystal and Tibetan bowls, rain sticks, bells, chimes, gongs and more while bathing in the healing energy all around you.

Sound healing activates the healing theta brain state and parasympathetic nervous system, releasing stress, quieting the mind and dropping into a deep state of well-being. The sound waves are resonant with the chakras, energy field and cells to support balance and alignment.

***As a special bonus, each person receives a crystal gift to hold during the sound bath and then take home to reconnect with energy of your personal experience!***

title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

A note about the format
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

title: The Science of Happiness: The Four Noble Truths
description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
The Science of Happiness: The Four Noble Truths with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich

**Sundays 8/16-9/13, 10:30am-11:45am**
Whether it’s everyday stress, sadness, or even anger, our suffering can be transformed into inner strength, love, and joy. The first step is understanding its source. In this series, we’ll explore Buddha’s teachings on the Four Noble Truths. The Four Noble Truths are the essence of Buddhist thought and gives us a clear, precise way to understand our life and how to move forward in it. Through teachings and meditation, we’ll discover that suffering comes not from external conditions, but from our own mind. Recognizing this opens the door to transforming our experience and uncovering a more lasting, genuine happiness.
Cost: $12 (free and online options for members)

title: On National Read a Book Day, Let's Walk at Lake Junaluska
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
September 6 is National Read a Book Day. Right before we step-off, let's share with each other the title of a book we recommend the others read too. If you are able to "show and tell" bring the book with you, so much the better. Don't worry, we'll give you time to put the book back in your car before we step-off on the walk. (I don't want to carry a book on a 7 KM walk with hills!)

Gather at 2:00 at Lake Junaluska inside the Bethea Welcome Center. This will be a 7 KM/4 mile route. The walk does not just go around the lake, but up to Lambuth Inn, along the Rose Walk, and through the Nature Garden. The view from Inspiration Point is a must-see!

Dress for the weather. Consider a hat and sunscreen. Some people may want walking poles, especially for the walk up to Lambuth Inn; tennis shoes should be fine. It is particularly important that walkers bring a protein snack and **plenty of** **water**. Restrooms are available at the Welcome Center, at Lambuth Inn, and along the route. Dogs on leash are welcome. Strollers are ok.

title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles!

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather, grab drinks and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. We want to know what you're reading! Organic dialogue welcome!

title: MST: Lane Pinnacle, 8 miles
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
Trailhead is Tanbark Tunnel on the BRP. From Tanbark Tunnel, we take the MST spur trail up to Rattlesnake Lodge and then the MST over Rich Knob, Wolf Den, and then up to Lane Pinnacle where we have views of the North Fork Reservoir and its surrounding watershed. Then we turn around and head back down.

Distance out and up is approximately 4 miles (8 miles round trip), and the elevation out and up is approximately 2,000 feet.

**2,000 feet elevation gain is no mean feat**. Most of the gain up to Rich Knob, about 1,700 feet, is in the first 2 miles--gives new meaning to the term "unrelenting." The rest is up and down to Lane Pinnacle. So . . . 2,000 feet up and 2,000 feet down over 8 miles.

**Car pool:** Meet at Folk Art Center, **lower parking level** at 8:30. Limited parking at the trail head.

**RELEASE OF LIABILITY:** The organizer of this trip is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this trip. If you sign up or participate in this event you acknowledge that you freely and voluntarily agree to assume all risks of injuries, illnesses, and damages arising from, as a result of, and associated with this event. title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**September 2026 Selection - *To Have and Have Not* by Ernest Hemingway**
[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Have-Not-Scribner-Classics/dp/0684859238/) - [GoodReads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/4630.To_Have_and_Have_Not)

*To Have and Have Not is the dramatic story of Harry Morgan, an honest man who is forced into running contraband between Cuba and Key West as a means of keeping his crumbling family financially afloat. His adventures lead him into the world of the wealthy and dissipated yachtsmen who throng the region and involve him in a strange and unlikely love affair.*

*In this harshly realistic, yet oddly tender and wise novel, Hemingway perceptively delineates the personal struggles of both the "haves" and the "have nots" and creates one of the most subtle and moving portraits of a love affair in his oeuvre. By turns funny and tragic, lively and poetic, remarkable in its emotional impact, To Have and Have Not is literary high adventure at its finest.*

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**Welcome to our monthly Book Club!** We’re a small, friendly group that gets together for fun, thoughtful conversations about a different book each month.

Finished the whole book? Great. Only made it through a few chapters? Still come. Didn’t read it at all but the discussion sounds interesting? Honestly, you’re welcome too.
We meet on the **first Tuesday of every month**.

One of the best things about this group is that we keep it relatively small and guide the conversation, so it doesn’t turn into three people talking while everyone else quietly questions their life choices. Everyone has a chance to jump in, share their thoughts, and explore the book’s characters, themes, writing, and bigger ideas.

You definitely don’t need to be a literary expert. Whether you read constantly or you’re trying to get back into it, this is a relaxed place to discover new books, hear different perspectives, and meet some great people along the way.

title: UnRuffle yo’self at Otter Hole
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
I am going to unravel my stress at Otter Hole Swimmin’ Hole at the headwaters of the So.Mills River.
Otter Hole is a small cascade dropping into a deep swimmin’ hole near the headwaters of the south fork of Mills River that flow out of Pink Beds watershed. We will pass some lovely rock walls, dripping and oozing water. We also pass some nice cascades and pools.
Difficulty: Forested single track moderate descent, ‘natural’ surface w/ rocks & roots.
The cold water of Otter Hole is suitable for deep water swimmin’ or floating.
We are the **Sloth Hike Team of WNC**: “We will get there when we get there.”
**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQ8H4EK2vt4**
Up to 12 ppl are welcome to join me.
I will spend (up to) 2-3 hours at the falls. Come prepared to pretend to meditate, ponderin’, practice your Tai-Chi, **森林浴**, read a book, prepare a meal, play a flute or swim.
**Hike Details:**
Social ‘hour’ at 9:50am. Bus leaves at 10:00a)
Length: 3.0mi RT; Accum ascent: 350 ft; most on the return. Pace: **1.5mph.**
**[Optional: Further down the trail is Billy Branch Falls (add 1 mi RT)]**
**Drive time: 30min/12 mi 1-way**
**Apprx return time: 2:30 PM (=4.25hrs)**
**Carpool contributions appreciated. $2.00 suggested**
**THIS IS A DOG-PARTICIPANT HIKE.** This event is NOT for those who are uncomfortable with the antics of fun-loving dogs. Well trained dogs (you don’t have to yell.) can be 'off-leash'. 'On leash' during the Unraveling (‘cept for swimmin’). Small (lap)dogs may carpool. Large dogs will drive themselves.
Weather Check: Brevard, NC
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
I currently have 2.5 driver. (=10ppl)
We suggest masks and open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others.
Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.
Incessant prattlers will be assumed to be having an affair. Obstreperous raucous yawping is discouraged.
**UnRuffle/UnRavel:** To experience a time of quiet in a manner that you feel worthwhile. Démêlez votre stress.
Engage the 5 senses (sight, smell, touch, taste, hearing),
Observe the movement of the forest & water.
Breathe the aroma of the air, water, plants and forest.
Feel the texture of the air, water, trees and plants.
Listening to the sound of air, water, critters & birds;
Taste the air of the breezes or soothing snacks.
All hikes are at your own risk. You are responsible for your OWN safety and adequate equipment.
Waiver: The organizer of this event is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this event. There are certain risks inherent in any outdoor activity. Each participant, by signing up to attend this event, agrees to release from liability the leader(s), Hendo Fun Friends, its Partners, Affiliates, and members for any accident, injury, illness, or personal loss which might occur while participating in this activity or while traveling in any vehicle during this trip. **Each participant further agrees to abide by the rules and regulations concerning safety, to follow instructions of the leader(s), and not to become intentionally separated from the group.** The leader(s) also has the right to use any images collected on this trip for recording on website photo collections.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

The Forsyte Saga - Volume 1 - 
John Galsworthy
description:
Books That Age Like Wine
We will only be reading “The Man of Property” but we can stay later and discuss the other two volumes if anyone is interested..

The three novels which make up The Forsyte Saga chronicle the ebbing social power of the commercial upper-middle class Forsyte family between 1886 and 1920. Galsworthy's masterly narrative examines not only their fortunes but also the wider developments within society, particularly the changing position of women. This is the only critical edition of the work available, with Notes that explain contemporary artistic and literary allusions and define the slang of the time.

title: Fall Wildflowers of the NC Arboretum
description:
Fall Wildflowers of the NC Arboretum
with Lauren Lampley 
Wednesday, September 9  |  1 – 4pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Core 
Register Here!
  
Interested in learning how to identify wildflowers? Join Lauren on this walk around the Arboretum property where we will go over different ways of identifying plants and different families of flowers. Some flowers are very difficult to identify to species and some are relatively easy so we will talk about how to get as close as possible with tools we can easily carry into the field. We will be using Newcomb’s guide to key out some of the less common flowers but will focus on learning how to look closely at flowers to identify them. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department. 
●  Members: Remember to enter your promo code upon checkout to receive your 10% member discount! Email adulteducation@ncarboretum.org with questions.

description:

Jenn will be teaching a new class at the beautiful Urban Oasis located 102 N. Lexington Ave. Asheville.
\~\~\~\~\~\~\~
Restorative Yoga is a deeply calming practice designed to support relaxation, recovery, and nervous system restoration. Using supportive props and gentle postures held for longer periods of time, this class encourages the body and mind to soften and fully unwind. Perfect for all levels seeking stillness, stress relief, and deep rest.

title: Plein Air Painting in the Gardens
description:
Plein Air Painting in the Gardens
with Erika Busse 
Thursday, September 10  |  9am – 11pm 
Register Here!
  
There is no better way to relax and connect with your creative side and nature than en plein air painting. In this class, artist Erika Busse will teach you how to paint an original Appalachian inspired artwork outside at the beautiful North Carolina Arboretum. She will take you through each step of the painting process, all skill levels are welcomed and all supplies are provided. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Erika Busse moved to Asheville in 2017 after graduating from the University of Alabama with degrees in art and business. She is a small business owner of her full time artist business, sharing mountain inspired painting and printmaking with the world. She has been teaching plein air painting classes since 2021.

title: Awakening Creativity  — An Introductory Workshop
description:
Awakening Creativity — An Introductory Workshop
With Catherine Willows 
Thursday, September 10  |  9:30 – 11:30 am 
Register Here!
  
Creativity lives innately within us all—our natural capacity to imagine, envision new possibilities, and bring fresh energy into our lives. In this two-hour introductory workshop, you’ll be invited into a different kind of art-making: not focused on skill or product, but on expression from within. 
Held in sacred space and in communion with nature, we’ll explore intuitive painting, journaling, and reflective practices to quiet the mind and awaken your inner creative self—helping you see what may not have been fully acknowledged, and allowing inspiration, clarity, and joy to arise. 
Many participants are surprised by what unfolds—the unexpected that emerges through the process itself. This introductory session lays the foundation for future workshops. 
No art experience is needed—just an open spirit and a willingness to explore and students are encouraged to bring their journals with them if they would like to. 
Catherine Willows is a Registered Nurse, Certified Functional Medicine Health Coach, and Transformational Creativity Coach, and founder of Willows Coaching and Consulting. While holding sacred space, she guides adults in awakening their inner creativity — moving beyond the demands of daily life into greater flow, self-discovery, and joy through intuitive art-making processes. Catherine believes creativity and our connection to the natural world are deeply interwoven  — both vital pillars of wellbeing, supporting nervous system regulation and inner equanimity, and together essential for living a meaningful, embodied life aligned with purpose and authentic expression.

📅 **Thursday, Sept 10th**
**⏰ 6:30 to 8:30 PM**
**📍 Top of the Monk, 92 Patton Ave, Asheville**

Summer is starting to wind down, so it seems like the perfect excuse to take Classy Cocktails upstairs, grab a great drink, enjoy a warm September evening on a rooftop, and hang out with some of our favorite people.

This time we're heading to Top of the Monk, downtown Asheville's oldest cocktail bar and one of those places that feels distinctly Asheville.

Tucked above the former Thirsty Monk (now Crowbar), Top of the Monk is an intimate cocktail lounge with a rooftop patio overlooking downtown and the Blue Ridge Mountains. And these folks take their cocktails seriously. They use fresh ingredients and make their own bitters, tinctures, infusions, syrups and shrubs in-house.

If whiskey is more your thing, you're in good hands there too. They have an impressive whiskey collection and bartenders who actually know what they're pouring.

And then there's the quirky little Top of the Monk tradition. Order a cocktail and you may receive a small key that unlocks one of their old post-office-box-style snack cubbies. You'll just have to come see what that's all about. 😉

**What to Expect**
**🍸** Really good handcrafted cocktails
🥃 Plenty of options for the whiskey lovers
🌄 Rooftop views over downtown and toward the mountains
☀️ One more gorgeous summer evening outside
😂 Easy conversation, laughs and the usual Classy Cocktails crew
😊 New faces are always welcome

We're keeping this one simple. Good people. Good drinks. A rooftop. A late-summer evening. Nowhere else you need to be for a couple of hours.

**Parking**
There are several paid parking lots around Top of the Monk, including parking directly behind it. The parking structure behind it, however, is only $1 an hour, so you shouldn't have to sacrifice your cocktail budget just to park your car. 😉

Come quench your thirst as we squeeze one more rooftop Classy Cocktails evening out of the summer. See you at the Top! 🍸🌄

title: BLUEGRASS JAM SPECIAL EDITION FEATURING THE DARREN NICHOLSON BAND
description:
A Grammy nominee and the winner of 13 International Bluegrass Music Association awards, Darren Nicholson has taken his own brand of mountain music around the world. A regular for years on the Grand Ole Opry and a founding member of acclaimed bluegrass group Balsam Range, Darren now spends his time recording, writing new songs, and performing original roots music inspired by the history & culture of his native Western North Carolina — homegrown, wholehearted music with a purpose.



A punchy mandolinist with instrumentation nods to Bill Monroe and Marty Stuart, Darren is also an introspective songwriter, technical harmony singer, convincing lead vocalist, and a man on a mission. His shows are a tailored experience — genuine, entertaining, and an extended handshake to the community., reflecting the fun-witted and approachable character formed in his raising.



Darren’s passion is sharing raw, honest-to-goodness, quality music with his audience. Music that’s good for his soul and theirs too. “That’s all I want,” says Darren. “I want to be a positive part of other people’s lives with music, you know? I want to be an ambassador to roots music – tip my hat to the past while looking forward at the same time. This music was intended to be played in a way that adds joy to the community. All I want is to restore that purpose, not to complete a transaction.” 



Darren says that when you come out to a show, whatever you do, please come talk afterward. “I’m like Willie Nelson. ‘I don’t want fans, I want friends.’ It’s a communal thing.” 



You can catch Darren almost every week sharing the music he loves somewhere, traveling both nationally and internationally — as a solo artist, in collaboration with other musicians, and with his own Darren Nicholson Band — a group of Appalachian musicians with a common respect for and love of American acoustic music who creatively blend bluegrass, folk, gospel, and swing into a new music experience. 



Doors at 6pm — show starts at 7pm. Suggested cover at the door. Open Jam follows at 9:30pm.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**[Sign-up opens Sunday, Sept. 6, 8:00 PM]**

This is an out-and-back hike on the Mountains-to-Sea Trail. Looking past the hurricane damage, there's the usual wooded beauty we've come to expect. As a bonus, this one's capped off with a lovely view at the turnaround point. Nearly all the elevation gain is in the first half of the trek -- not advisable unless you know you can handle an 800-ft climb spread across two miles. Difficulty level 3.5 out of 10 on my highly subjective scale.

We'll keep a humane pace on the uphill, take a 15-minute snack break at the vista point midway, and then head back for an easy downhill return.

Dogs are welcome but must be leashed according to Forest Service regulations.

**MEETING TIME & DIRECTIONS**

We'll head out from the parking lot at **9** **AM** at the Folk Art Center on the Blue Ridge Parkway. The entrance road is near Milepost 383. Please arrive a few minutes early for sign-in and introductions.

On Google Maps: [https://goo.gl/maps/85AQ8VhC1pByMCSC8](https://goo.gl/maps/85AQ8VhC1pByMCSC8)

You'll pass the front of the building on your right. Keep going to the **second parking area** furthest from the building. Look for me and my car -- a silver Hyundai.

**COURTESY TO WAIT-LISTERS (Please!)**

Only sign up if you \*truly\* plan to come. If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible so wait-listers will have sufficient notice. (The same goes if you're on the waitlist and know you can't attend. Please change to "Not Going.") And please please PLEASE don't be a no-show.

**WEATHER**

I'll watch the weather and post a cancellation message by 7:30 AM if the forecast is >50% chance of precipitation.

**GUESTS**

If you'd like to bring a guest, please have them join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike on their own.

title: River Systems of the Blue Ridge
description:
River Systems of the Blue Ridge
with Anton DuMars 
Friday, September 11  |  12 – 4pm 
BRN – Core 
Register Here!
  
Water is essential to life but is also a powerful agent of change. Rivers, through both daily processes and catastrophic floods, shape Earth’s surface through erosion and sediment transport. In River Systems of the Blue Ridge, we will investigate how the Broad River changes character and shapes the landscape along its course from the headwaters, through the Piedmont, and onto the Atlantic Ocean. 
Anton DuMars, a resident of Black Mountain, NC, is an adjunct professor at the College of Charleston. His geological interests include fluvial, deltaic, and coastal processes. Ideally, he’s spending time on a hiking trail or aboard his sailboat.

title: History and Archaeology of the Arboretum
description:
History and Archaeology of the Arboretum
with Bob and Mary Noel 
Friday, September 11  |  1 – 4pm 
Register Here!
  
The land that makes up The North Carolina Arboretum has been home to different human groups over a span of more than 15,000 years. It has had many uses and been shaped by those who lived here. This walk, led by archaeologists Bob and Mary Noel, will give participants a chance to see and hear about past occupants of this land, and even a little history about how it became the state’s Arboretum. 
Bob and Mary Noel both had long careers as archaeologists with the US Forest Service. Bob worked mostly in North Carolina where he recorded thousands of sites on national forest lands here. Most of Mary’s archaeological work was in Idaho and Ohio. Both of them have been active in living history programs as well, most recently with the Heritage Alliance in Jonesborough, Tennessee. The Noels now have a consulting firm and still do archaeological survey projects. Mary can be found working at the Arboretum’s Baker Information desk several days a week, sharing her knowledge of local trails, gardens and history.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Learn to Swing Dance + 2 Hours of Social Dancing
description:
Asheville 20s-40s Social Group
Let's go to Asheville Swing Night on Friday Sept 11th for an evening of swing dancing, great music, and a fun beginner-friendly lesson. 💃🕺

The instructors (Jared & Marguerite) will kick things off at 7PM with the beginner fundamentals so everyone can learn the basic footwork and get comfortable with swing dancing. 🎶

No partner needed. During both the lesson and social dance, most people rotate partners, making it a fun way to meet people and get comfortable in the space.

(Most people come alone, by the way.)

**What dance are we learning?**
Intro Lindy Hop and East Coast Swing.

**How many people will be there?**
Throughout the night there are usually 50–70 people who attend. The lesson and dance is open to the public, not just this Meetup group.

**What should I wear?**
Wear shoes that are comfortable to dance in. Heels are not recommended. Leather-soled shoes or comfortable sneakers are best. Dressing up is optional — people wear everything from casual to vintage-inspired outfits.

**Does the Meetup group sit together all evening?**
Once the lesson starts, the Meetup group disperses to take the lesson with everyone else. The lesson is immediately followed by a social dance. In our experience, some of the Meetup attendees continue to sit together, chat, and listen to the music. Others (including the hosts) will be gone dancing and mingling around the room.

**Logistics**
📍 Location: Haw Creek Commons
Parking is onsite, or at Haw Creek Elementary if the parking lot is full. Just walk across the field to the venue.

🕖 7PM sharp — Beginner swing dance lesson
(Please arrive on time, as the lesson builds progressively and is harder to join late if you're brand new.)

💃🕺 8-10:00PM — Social dance with DJ

title: Stacy Antonel
description:
Imagine Tammy Wynette crossed with the Ventures and you’ll have an idea of the sonic world of Americana artist Stacy Antonel’s forthcoming EP, The Seahorses: Volume 1. Always a genre-defying artist, Antonel blends her passion for classic country, jazz and surf rock with this collection of songs, and the result is a fresh hybrid of musical styles that feels both vintage and hyper-modern. Recorded at Nashville’s Fitting Room Studio, the band includes heavy hitters Ethan Ballinger (Miranda Lambert), Joe Reed (Merle Haggard), Paul Sgroi (Josh Hedley) and San Diego jazz phenom Tony Econom. 



Antonel grew up in a seaside San Diego town called Ocean Beach, listening to pop and R&B hits and studying classical piano until she was eighteen. She cites an eclectic range of artists as her earliest musical inspirations: Tori Amos for her peculiar phrasing and distinct songwriting, Otis Redding for his rich, emotive vocal delivery. After graduating from UC Berkeley, she moved to Buenos Aires, where she answered a Craigslist ad for a singer who sounds like June Carter Cash, and contributed vocals to several jingles for MTV and Jeep that aired throughout Latin America. She sang in a friend’s electro-cumbia band for a while before returning to California, where she started singing professionally at weddings, bars, and local venues. But it wasn’t until discovering country music that she felt at home. “One day I randomly bought a bunch of 99 cent country records and fell in love with the genre; the concision of the writing, the wit, how it doesn’t take itself too seriously even while dealing with deep subject matter.” 



Antonel’s debut album Always the Outsider, released in 2022, blends elements of mid-century country music with unconventional subject matter and virtuosic instrumentation– including tracks with Doug Pettibone (Lucinda Williams) on pedal steel and acoustic guitar. The thematically unique collection explores metaphysical and supernatural concepts (alien-earthling romance, past-life trauma) as well as grounded narratives of everyday experience (isolation, disconnectedness, sexual desire, feeling like an alien in your own body). Always the Outsider was critically praised, netting coverage in publications from Holler Country to The Bluegrass Situation, and was hailed as a 2022 Essential Album by Saving Country Music.Music 8:30-11:30pm $10 cover at the door.

title: Forest Bathing: A Harvest Season Retreat
description:
Forest Bathing: A Harvest Season Retreat
with Asheville Wellness Tours 
Saturday, September 12  |  10am – 1pm 
Register Here!
  
Celebrate abundance, balance and equilibrium during this immersive morning nature connection retreat. During this seasonal transition, we’ll mark the threshold between summer and fall, honoring the Earth’s bountiful harvest while slowing our pace, awakening our senses, and practicing embodied acts of gratitude. Honoring this liminal fifth season, connecting with ourselves, each other, and the more-than-human-world, nourishing the relationships that sustain and connect us. 
Your guide, Christa Hebal, will lead you on a gentle journey through the forest, weaving mindfulness, breathwork, forest bathing and nature therapy together for a restorative morning on some of the trails less traveled at the North Carolina Arboretum. We’ll celebrate the experience with a community Earth offering, followed by a wild-foraged tea ceremony and snacks. Bring an open mind and an open heart. All are welcome. Presented through Adult & Continuing Education Programs in collaboration with Asheville Wellness Tours. 
Christa Hebal is a certified Nature and Forest Therapy Guide by the Association of Nature and Forest Therapy. Born and raised in the mountains of northeast Tennessee, she has lived in Asheville for 24 years. Christa has an adventurous heart, and loves to help others encounter wholeness through embodiment and nature connection practices. She has had a professional bodywork practice for 18 years as a nationally certified Massage Therapist, and is also a practitioner of Ortho-Bionomy®, Usui Reiki Master, Certified Pediatric Massage Therapist, Clinical Aromatherapist, and Certified Traditional Herbalist. She is also certified in CPR and Wilderness First Aid.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: The Transformative Power of Love: Empowerment of Buddha Maitreya
description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
The Transformative Power of Love: Empowerment of Buddha Maitreya with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich

Love is the key to a happy and meaningful life. When we have a strong loving mind, our whole experience of the world changes - our life fills with hope, our relationships become stronger, and we naturally contribute to a more positive world.
Buddha Maitreya is the embodiment of loving kindness of all the Buddhas. The empowerment is a blissful guided meditation that connects us to Maitreya’s enlightened love awakening our own potential to develop the universal love of a Buddha. By receiving his inspiring blessings we can swiftly actualize our own potential for love and gain the confidence we need to progress along the spiritual path.
***“An empowerment bestows upon us special blessings that heal our mental continuum and awaken our Buddha nature.”***
*— Venerable Geshe Kelsang Gyatso Rinpoche*
In the commentary, we will learn the special brief practice of Buddha Maitreya. Through identifying strongly with this Buddha’s qualities, we nurture them within ourselves; in this way we begin to become someone whose love transforms the world.
An empowerment is a special ceremony in which we receive the blessings that heal our mental continuum and awaken our Buddha nature. It consists of meditations, guided visualizations and prayers followed by a teachings to explain the practice. Everybody Welcome.
Cost $70

title: Sep 12th An Evening of Spicy/Sensual Snuggles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space. use the link below to reserve your ticket-
https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/sep-12th-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles

What is a Sensual Snuggle Event?\*\*
This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch. We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, kiss, expose nipples, play, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

**Our Agreements:**
1- We ask for what we want an wait for a yes before touching others.
2- We say no if we don’t want to do something.
3- We try to receive a no with grace and not take it personally.
4- We arrive on time, clean (as scent free as possible), and sober.
5- We keep our pants/shorts on at this event. (Tops are optional; this is a sensual space, not a sexual space.)
6- We are here to connect with others. Connection can be verbal, platonic, or spicy!
7- We welcome diversity. Isms and Phobias are not welcome here!

**Who should attend:**
People who are interested in safely exploring touch and sensuality with strangers. This includes people who are single, people who are not single, couples, folks who are new to town and looking for connection, people of all/any genders and sexual orientations, people of all ages (18 and up). People who understand and respect consent, who will take care of themselves and people around them. This event is queer-normative. The guest list will include all genders, orientations, ages, and personalities. If that’s not your thing… This is not the event for you.
***Who should NOT attend:***
-People who are only looking for a sex party.
-People who do not understand and respect consent.
-People who have extreme fear of setting and speaking their personal boundaries; in order to create a safe space we need to know that you will say “no” if you feel a no.
-People who are homophobic, racist, sexist, ageist, ableist…
-People under 18 years of age.
***Schedule of the Evening***

\*6:50pm Doors Open, Mix & Mingle

* 7:00pm We gather in a circle to meet each other, build a container, cover consent and boundary setting and discuss event agreements. Then we will play a few intimacy building games to meet and connect with other people in the room. Please make sure you arrive on-time!
\*8:15pm Once the container is built we will have self directed snuggling and sensual interactions until the end of the party.
* 10:50pm Closing Circle; a time to re-center and connect as a group to verbally share anything that came up at the event or to voice gratitude to someone(s) you enjoyed interacting with.
\*11:00pm cleanup & head home; you are welcome to help.

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

These events are not "gender balanced"[. Check out our website for more information about this decision.](http://holdmeavl.com/why-i-dont-gender-balance-events/)

**Simple definitions/clarifications-** Platonic- marked by the absence of romance or sex.
Most of the interactions we have with friends and strangers are platonic.
Sensual- gratification of the senses or the indulgence of appetite.
We might feel sensual when we feel someone's breath on our neck or experience a extra long and slow caress.
Sexual- having or involving sex.
Often involving one more more peoples genitals; perhaps seeking orgasm.
\*Refund Policy- Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid. Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event. No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

Asheville Movement Collective
Sunday, September 13th
1st Dance Wave 8:30\-10:30am \| Warmup 8:30am \| Opening Circle 9am
2nd Dance Wave 10:30\-12:30am \| Warmup 10:30am \| Opening Circle 11am
Facilitator Rory Jagdeo

Intention: Dance Medicine

Dance Medicine \~ Anonymous
This is the medicine each of us needs
To come awake and be healed
To be emptied and refilled
With joy
With hope
With courage
With love
For our own selves
So we can become the medicine
For the world

## About Rory Jagdeo

Rory is a singer/songwriter and an AMC Facilitator. He stepped into Ecstatic Dance in Houston, TX for the first time in 2014 and believes in the power of dance to transform and bring a healthier, happier, and connected lifestyle. It is that driving force and passion that pushes him to explore the role of being an Ecstatic Dance Facilitator using world rhythms and different musical genres to weave mixes that incorporate many elements of 8Rhythms.

title: The Science of Happiness: The Four Noble Truths
description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
The Science of Happiness: The Four Noble Truths with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich

**Sundays 8/16-9/13, 10:30am-11:45am**
Whether it’s everyday stress, sadness, or even anger, our suffering can be transformed into inner strength, love, and joy. The first step is understanding its source. In this series, we’ll explore Buddha’s teachings on the Four Noble Truths. The Four Noble Truths are the essence of Buddhist thought and gives us a clear, precise way to understand our life and how to move forward in it. Through teachings and meditation, we’ll discover that suffering comes not from external conditions, but from our own mind. Recognizing this opens the door to transforming our experience and uncovering a more lasting, genuine happiness.
Cost: $12 (free and online options for members)

title: Inner Child Playshop
description:
Senseful Soul’s Asheville Healing Community🧘🏻‍♀️🏳️‍🌈🪐🔮
You're invited to the best play date of the year.
Who's inviting you? Your inner child. And they want you to know; it's been too long since the two of you spent time together doing things that bring you joy and wonder.

Senseful Wellness is pairing up with Ayla Claypool for an afternoon that is equal parts intentional and delightfully unserious. A three-hour hang designed for the part of you that still knows how to play.
Ayla will guide everyone through a series of games using techniques from physical theatre theorist Jacques Lecoq in order to open our spacial and emotional awareness and take steps toward transformation. Exploratory and silly, serious play asks everyone the question of what does it mean to move like a kid again. To find the joy.

Vi will open and close the Playshop calling in your inner child and creating the container for them to actually show up and stay a while.

Jenn will move everyone through an Inner Child Vinyasa Flow, designed for all bodies and all ages.
Together we have created an afternoon that gives your inner child permission to flourish, and reminds everyone that we are all still big kids at heart.

Come play with us.

his relationships with his contemporaries and
his ongoing artistic legacy.
The film invites audiences to intimately examine
Michelangelo’s art and artistic process – from the
Carrara quarries where Michelangelo sourced his
marble, to the new technology being used to
attribute works. The film also offers a rare
chance to get up close to the mesmerizing
Rothschild Bronzes, which, following an
extensive research project carried out by
Academics in Cambridge in 2015, were positively
attributed to Michelangelo after over a century of debate.

title: Sep 13th Queer Platonic Cuddles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
**[REGISTER HERE](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/sep-13th-4-7pm-queer-platonic-cuddles-tranzmission-benefit)**[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/sep-13th-4-7pm-queer-platonic-cuddles-tranzmission-benefit)(rsvp's on Meetup do not count as registering)
This event is a fundraiser for Tranzmission. 100% of ticket sales go directly to them!

This is an event for Adults who identify as LGBTQIA+.
The intention of this event is to build community and provide a supportive place for participants to explore sweet platonic physical touch.
No one turned away for lack of funds (please ask if you truly need a scholarship or work trade).
**This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch.** We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

Consent and respect are at the forefront of the experience. We strive for a safe and welcoming environment, fostering a sense of trust that allows attendees to fully enjoy shared touch without any pressure or expectations.

Discover the joy of shared vulnerability in an environment where your authenticity is not just accepted but celebrated. This event is an opportunity to connect with like-minded individuals who appreciate the simplicity of human touch and the profound impact it can have on our well-being.

Express yourself in a way that feels true to you, whether through cozy attire or a touch of personal flair. We encourage individuality and self-expression, creating an inclusive space where everyone can be their authentic selves. Dress code is Casual and cozy.

This event will be indoors. Masks are optional. DO NOT ATTEND if you or someone you are physically close with is sick.

This is an inclusive environment where we will aim to foster the dismantling of and no tolerance of ableism, fat-shaming, homophobia/transphobia, sexism, xenophobia, classism, racism & other ideas that lead to folks feeling disconnected or unwelcome.

**THE RULES**
1\. Pants stay on for the whole event\.
2\. You do not have to touch anyone at this event\.
3\. You must ask permission and receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone\. Please be specific in your requests\.
4\. If you feel a yes\, say YES\. If you feel a no\, say NO\. If you’re a maybe\, say NO\. You can always change your mind\.
5\. Get your facilitator if you have a question or concern\, or if you need assistance with anything during the event\.
6\. Talking\, laughter\, silence\, silliness\, stillness\, and crying are welcome\.

**ETIQUETTE**

* ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle.
* Please be free of strong scents; many folks would rather not be close to someone who smells of perfume, essential oils, or cigarettes
* BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share. The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

We take individual and group safety seriously! if you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at a touch based event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy- Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid. Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event. No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.
